## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3 (titled *Akālacīvara*) regulates the storage of extra robe-cloth by Buddhist monastics [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that if a monk receives robe-cloth and retains it with the expectation of obtaining additional material to complete a set, he may keep the cloth for up to one month; keeping it beyond that period requires him to forfeit the robe-cloth and confess the transgression [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

This precept belongs to the common disciplinary core of early Buddhist monasticism. Curated parallels on SuttaCentral show corresponding rules across nearly all major Vinaya lineages, including the Bhikkhu Pātimokkhas and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, alongside an early Gāndhārī fragment and counterpart rules in the Bhikkhunī Vinayas (e.g., Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 15) [SuttaCentral]. Computational alignments from DharmaNexus confirm these affiliations, identifying direct correspondences with Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* texts and Tibetan Vinaya collections (notably the *Vinayavibhaṅga*, D0003-2, and the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha*, D0007) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects extensive shared phrasing with related robe and forfeiture rules, including Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules 1, 2, 23, 28, and 29, the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), the *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8), and later Vinaya commentaries such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. The reference passages identified in secondary literature offer no direct analysis, consisting only of a misplaced volume/heading reference and a bare index entry [1, 2].
